newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso holds cash-strapped elections.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso holds cash-strapped elections.

text.p: Burkina Faso holds national assembly elections on Sunday in which only President Blaise Compaore's ruling party can afford to put up candidates nationwide.
Polling is scheduled to begin at 8 a.m. (0800 GMT) in the landlocked West African state and will continue until 6 p.m. (1800 GMT), the electoral commission said.

Short of funds, the electoral commission borrowed ballot boxes from neighbouring Ghana. Former colonial power France sent indelible ink to ensure nobody votes twice in the second elections since a return to multi-party politics in the 1990s.
Among 13 competing parties, only the ruling Congress for Popular Democracy (CDP) has candidates in all 45 districts. No opposition party has sufficient funds to contest that many.
The CDP holds 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, elected in 1992.
A total of 569 candidates are standing, 80 of them women.
Opposition parties, short of cash, have been forced to stage modest campaigns instead of holding big public meetings and the ruling party heads into the poll confident of keeping its majority.
"A grassroots campaign is a campaign of truth, because we don't have the funds we need and we don't make promises," said Ram Ouedraogo, chairman of the opposition Burkina Faso Ecologist Party.
The CDP, which held more than 100 rallies in the Ouagadougou area alone during the campaign, says it is confident of victory and has no need to resort to its position of power to assure victory.
Opposition parties are less sure after making allegations of widespread malpractice and fraud at the last election.

"We have to hope that those who last time put a lot more effort into fraud than into fair competition will be more above board this time," said Sebastian Ouedraogo, secretary general of the opposition Alliance for Democracy and Federation recently.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 military coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.

Under pressure from Western donors for democratic reform in the early 1990s, Compaore underwent a lightning conversion to multi-party politics and was elected as the sole candidate in 1991 elections -- which opposition parties boycotted as unfair.
In January, parliament voted an amendment to the constitution allowing him to stand for a second seven-year term of office in 1998 and beyond.

Burkina Faso, locked in the arid Sahel belt, exports livestock to its neighbours and increasing quantities of green beans and other fruit and vegetables to Europe. Gold mining is on the rise and plans are afoot to mine zinc and manganese.
